title: Block periodization of endurance training - a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Mølmen KS, Øfsteng SJ, Rønnestad BR
journal: Open Access Journal of Sports Medicine
population: Trained to well-trained endurance athletes in block-periodized (BP) versus traditional (TRAD) training; 2905 studies screened, 20 records included, 6 pooled
findings: Of 2905 studies screened, 20 records met eligibility criteria; 6 were pooled for VO2max and maximal power output (Wmax).
Meta-analysis showed small favourable effects for BP versus TRAD for VO2max (SMD 0.40, 95% CI 0.02 to 0.79) and Wmax (SMD 0.28, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.54).
For endurance performance and workload at thresholds, BP generally showed moderate to large effect sizes versus TRAD.
Authors call BP an adequate alternative to TRAD but urge caution because of small studies of generally low methodological quality (mean PEDro 3.7/10).
limitations: Few small, low-quality studies (mean PEDro 3.7/10); lower CI bounds are essentially zero; full text shows no running studies (cyclists and skiers dominate: 'runner' absent, 'cyclist' 22 mentions, 'skier' 16); no ultra-distance data.
implications: Offer block-style mesocycles (concentrated interval block then lower-intensity weeks) as an optional, flagged-experimental template for trained athletes, not a default or for beginners.
Default to traditional progression; no numeric block parameter is justified by this evidence.

verification.notes: Crossref title is HTML-wrapped; journal, 2019, authors match. Numbers verified in PubMed abstract. Sport mix claim checked against PMC6802561 full text. Evidence level downgraded A to B because of poor primary-study quality.
